chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would not slaughter one sheep while watching another being slaughtered, nor slaughter a large camel while watching another being slaughtered.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on showing an animal another being slaughtered before its turn?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) emphasis on *ihsan* (excellence) in ritual slaughter by preventing the animal from witnessing the slaughter of its peer, thereby reducing psychological distress. This practice reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of extending mercy (*rahma*) to animals as part of the spiritual discipline of the believer, ensuring the act is performed with calmness and dignity rather than haste or cruelty.
